{"grade":6,"complete":false,"main_gap":"The set Q is wrongly defined as primes dividing A; the argument requires Q to be all primes at most A.","errors":[{"description":"With the stated Q, sigma(x)=P(x) need not hold when all prime factors of x are at most A. Likewise, P(x)\sigma(x) may contain primes below A. These false claims invalidate the key lemma and periodicity deduction. Replacing Q by all primes p≤A repairs the proof.","quote":"Let
\[
Q=\{p:p\text{ is prime and }p\mid A\},
\qquad
\sigma(x)=P(x)\cap Q.
\]"}],"notes":"This appears to be a localized definition error: the later discussion explicitly identifies the intended finite set as all primes at most A. With that correction, the induction and the global translation-periodicity argument are complete."}
